objective.title: Traverse reconnaissance
objective.task: Prepare a Moon or Mars rover route reconnaissance method by comparing regional slopes and relief at two or more stops.
objective.supports: Regional terrain variation and a repeatable remote reconnaissance workflow.
objective.unresolved: Wheel traction, bearing capacity, small obstacles and autonomous perception require field measurements.
objective.next: Acquire rover-scale stereo or lidar and measure traction before choosing a field traverse.

roughness.method: Media de gamma0 VV (RTC, aplanada por terreno) en dB sobre la ventana 2400 m (240×240 px a 10 m, vecino más próximo); desviación típica 2.39 dB. Proxy de rugosidad superficial a escala de la longitud de onda banda C (~5.6 cm), no rugosidad geométrica medida. Escena única 2026-11-12, órbita descending.

environment.scope: Site/window environmental context, not a stop measurement; acquisition time is independent of SIM elapsed time.

decision.rationale: 1/2 planned stops inspected; coverage is incomplete. Complete or revise the traverse before advancing.
strengths: Regional terrain variation and a repeatable remote reconnaissance workflow.
Source-linked regional DEM and traceable stop coordinates.
breakdowns: Wheel traction, bearing capacity, small obstacles and autonomous perception require field measurements.
DEM elevations and slopes describe regional terrain; interpolation adds no detail. No sub-DEM rocks, safe zones or soil measurements are inferred.
Comparable topography is not planetary similarity or field feasibility. Earth gravity, atmosphere, radiation, water and biology differ from Moon and Mars conditions.
Rover motion, payload activity and battery use are illustrative SIM models; no spacecraft descent or target telemetry is generated.
nextSteps: Review the uninspected legs, revise constraints or acquire missing terrain data, then repeat the campaign.
Choose an independently documented planetary reference and audit scale, geology and environmental differences.
Confirm permits, access, field safety and instrument calibration with local specialists.

limitations: An Earth remote reconnaissance simulation, not a field visit or mission certification.
DEM elevations and slopes describe regional terrain; interpolation adds no detail. No sub-DEM rocks, safe zones or soil measurements are inferred.

Rover motion, payload activity and battery use are illustrative SIM models; no spacecraft descent or target telemetry is generated.
Stop arrival tolerance (5 m) is a simulated position threshold, not DEM accuracy or an instrument footprint.
Earth session only; no destination landing or M2 tracking context.
